QF.id: Clubbing, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses_13

question.text: Mr. Girish has three minor children. The income from investments in their names is: Child 1 — Rs.8,000, Child 2 — Rs.12,000, Child 3 — Rs.5,000. Girish's income is Rs.15,00,000 and his wife's income is Rs.6,00,000. What is the total amount clubbed with Girish's income after exemption?

answer.text: Rs.25,000 — full income of all three children clubbed with Girish
Rs.20,500 — total Rs.25,000 minus Rs.1,500 exemption per child (Rs.4,500 total)
Rs.23,500 — total Rs.25,000 minus Rs.1,500 exemption for only one child
Rs.21,500 — total Rs.25,000 minus Rs.1,500 exemption for two children only (third child not eligible)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 64(1A) of the Income Tax Act, the investment income of a minor child is clubbed with the parent having the higher total income. Girish (Rs.15,00,000) earns more than his wife (Rs.6,00,000), so all three children's income is clubbed with him. Total minor income = Rs.8,000 + Rs.12,000 + Rs.5,000 = Rs.25,000. Section 10(32) provides an exemption of Rs.1,500 per child per year, applied to each child separately with no cap on the number of children, giving Rs.1,500 x 3 = Rs.4,500. Net amount added to Girish's income = Rs.25,000 - Rs.4,500 = Rs.20,500. The Trap: Option A forgets the per-child Section 10(32) exemption entirely. Option C applies the exemption only once for the family instead of once per child. Option D invents a "two-child" limit that doesn't exist in Section 10(32) — the exemption is genuinely available for every minor child whose income is clubbed. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages reviewed in the audit support that minor income is clubbed with a parent/guardian under Section 64 (with a disability exception), but the specific Rs.1,500 per-child Section 10(32) exemption, the higher-income-parent rule, and the no-two-child cap are not on the pages checked. The figures above reflect the standard provisions of the Income Tax Act as generally applied in industry practice.
